text:
Alex: thinking out loud — we need to expose low-bit kernel selection + quantization knobs in the SDK (fp8/int8/4bit + presets). Had a weird perf regression after the fp8 pilot and want to avoid shipping surprises. Thoughts on defaults and safety rails?
Maria: can you paste the profiling numbers and where you saw the regression?
Alex: quick summary from the canary run (shortened):
```
model: redwood-small-v2
hardware: a100-40GB
baseline (fp16): median token/s = 96, p95 latency = 42ms
fp8-canary: median token/s = 118 (good for batching), p95 latency = 58ms (worse for short seq)
kv-cache hit path: latency +12ms in fp8 due to extra quant->float conversions
issue: bursty chat with cache hits regressed overall latency
```
Ryan: noted — we've seen the same pattern. fp8 kernels are faster on sustained large batches, but for small single-client requests the kernel selection + quantization conversion overhead (and sometimes fallback kernels) kills p95. KV cache indexing sometimes forces a decode path.
Jen: core question: what params do we want in the SDK? my suggestion: expose a small surface: `quant.mode` (auto|fp16|fp8|int8|4bit), `quant.preset` (conservative|balanced|aggressive), `quant.calibration` (offline|auto-warmup|none), and safety rails like `quant.min_quality` and `quant.allow_fallback`.
Sam: prototype SDK config I sketched — happy to iterate:
```
"quant": {
  "mode": "auto",
  "preset": "balanced",
  "calibration": "offline",
  "min_quality": "0.98",
  "allow_fallback": true
}
```
Maria: two quick concerns: 1) `auto` calibration that does warmup runs will add extra cost and startup latency — not OK for ephemeral hosted calls by default. 2) we need clear server-side guards: if quality (eval set) drops more than X% vs baseline then force fallback.
Ryan: also KV cache behavior — runtime should be able to prefer a kernel that avoids conversion in the hot cache path. Suggest adding kernel selection heuristics: prefer kernel K that keeps KV cache in native dtype for cached layers, otherwise prefer fp16 for low-latency small-reqs.
Alex: agreed. UX: expose presets + an expandable advanced section. Default: `balanced` (safe perf wins, conservative calibration). Document that `aggressive` enables int8/4bit and may reduce quality; require explicit opt-in. Add server guard: `server_quality_gate_pct=95` (if eval metric <95% baseline -> fallback).
infra-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary rollout for runtime v2.14 with fp8 kernels at 2026-03-31T10:00Z (canary=10% -> monitor).
Sam: we'll need telemetry to make this fold: emit `quant_mode`, `kernel_choice`, `kv_hit_latency`, `calibration_type` per route. Then add an automated eval job that runs a small prompt set and flags regressions.
Jen: doc wording suggestion — short, actionable: "Presets control tradeoffs between latency and quality. 'balanced' (default) — prefer stable quality; 'aggressive' — enables low-bit kernels and requires explicit QA. Calibration must be run for int8/4bit; offline recommended."
Alex: next steps: Ryan add runtime kernel heuristic to prefer KV-safe kernels; Sam add SDK param + preset enum PR; Jen write docs and opt-in copy; Maria define quality gate thresholds and CI eval job; I'll coordinate canary and monitor dashboards. :thumbsup:
Ryan: i'll open PR for telemetry + kernel heuristics this afternoon.
Maria: i'll draft the eval job query and baseline numbers.
Alex: thanks all — short followups in PRs.
